title: The Only Unsolved Hijacking in US History
description:
In 1971, a man in a suit hijacked a plane, collected $200,000 in cash, and jumped out over the Pacific Northwest. He was never seen again.

HistoryLink.org's account of the 1980 ransom money discovery

scenes.text: In 1971, a hijacker jumped out of a moving passenger plane with two hundred thousand dollars in cash -- and was never seen again.
On 24/11/1971, a man calling himself Dan Cooper boarded a flight from Portland to Seattle in a plain business suit.
Mid-flight, he handed a flight attendant a note. He had a bomb, and wanted two hundred thousand dollars and four parachutes.
The airline paid. Cooper released all thirty six passengers in Seattle, then ordered the plane back into the air, heading for Mexico.
Somewhere over the dense forests of southwest Washington, he lowered the plane's rear stairs and jumped into a storm, alone, at night.
No body, no parachute, nothing. To this day, it's the only unsolved commercial hijacking in US history.
In 1980, a boy playing by the Columbia River dug up three rotting bundles of cash. Only 294 of the ten thousand bills were ever recovered.
If he survived that jump, where do you think Cooper actually landed?
